name: dns01-delegated-subdomain-challenge-fails
query: cert-manager Issuer with Cloudflare DNS-01 against `prod.example.com` keeps failing: `presenting challenge: NS lookup found no answer for _acme-challenge.prod.example.com`. The API token has `Zone:DNS:Edit` on `example.com`. Records I create manually via dashboard work fine. What's wrong?

files.issuer.yaml:
apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: Issuer
metadata:
  name: letsencrypt-prod
spec:
  acme:
    server: https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
    email: ops@example.com
    privateKeySecretRef:
      name: letsencrypt-prod
    solvers:
      - dns01:
          cloudflare:
            apiTokenSecretRef:
              name: cloudflare-api-token
              key: api-token

expected_behavior: Identifies two likely root causes and gives diagnostics for each. (1) Delegated subdomain: if `prod.example.com` is a separate Cloudflare zone (or NS-delegated to another provider), the token scoped to `example.com` cannot write `_acme-challenge.prod.example.com` in the `prod.example.com` zone. Diagnostic: `dig +trace prod.example.com NS` to see which zone is authoritative. (2) Propagation delay: cert-manager checks the record from public resolvers before Cloudflare has propagated globally; the message text 'NS lookup found no answer' is consistent with this.

For (1), the fix: re-create the token with `Zone:DNS:Edit` scoped to the actual subzone (`prod.example.com`). Do NOT use 'All Zones' as a shortcut — over-scoped tokens violate least-privilege and the SKILL.md explicitly forbids this.

For (2), gives the cert-manager `cnameStrategy: Follow` pattern — point `_acme-challenge.prod.example.com` to a CNAME in a zone the token CAN write (e.g., `_acme-challenge.prod.example.com CNAME _acme-challenge.delegated.example.com`), then write to the CNAME target instead. Useful when you can't scope the token to the subzone.
Concrete diagnostic command: `dig +trace _acme-challenge.prod.example.com TXT @1.1.1.1` after cert-manager presents — confirms whether the record exists in authoritative DNS.
Does NOT recommend the deprecated Global API Key as a workaround.
Does NOT suggest switching to HTTP-01 unless the user has constraints that DNS-01 specifically solves (wildcards, private/internal services).
